name: CS-Cart
title: CS-Cart SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on CS-Cart: 20 of 43 services wired. Browsing and cart work, but there is no shopper sign-in and the storefront cannot complete an order.
lede: The CS-Cart connector covers browsing and the cart through CS-Cart’s REST API, which has no checkout resource and no shopper sign-in. It authenticates every call with an admin’s e-mail and API key.
verdict: Shoppers can browse and fill a cart, but cannot sign in, and the storefront cannot complete an order. CS-Cart’s REST API has no checkout resource; the one call that creates an order sits in the connector’s `orderService.codCheckout()`, which the storefront’s payment step does not call, so every way it places an order throws `NotSupportedError`.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your CS-Cart store

env.name: PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_URL
env.note: Your CS-Cart store’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_KEY
env.note: Despite the name, an admin’s e-mail address — the HTTP Basic username. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_SECRET
env.note: The API key generated for that admin in the CS-Cart admin panel — the HTTP Basic password.

env.name: PUBLIC_CS_CART_STORE_ID
env.note: Company ID for company-scoped routes on CS-Cart Ultimate and Multi-Vendor, such as `/api/stores/{id}/orders`. `PUBLIC_CS_CART_CHANNEL_ID` is read if it is unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_CS_CART_CHANNEL_ID
env.note: Read as the company ID when `PUBLIC_CS_CART_STORE_ID` is unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/cs-cart-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_CS_CART_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_CS_CART_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `PUBLIC_CS_CART_ACCESS_KEY`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Generate an API key for an admin in the CS-Cart admin panel — and read the limitations before putting it anywhere a browser can see.
howItWorks: CS-Cart has one REST surface under two version prefixes, authenticated with HTTP Basic: an admin’s e-mail as the username and their generated API key as the password. On CS-Cart Ultimate and Multi-Vendor many routes are company-scoped, and the connector reads the company ID from the store variable rather than assuming `1`.

There is no checkout entity in the REST API: payment methods are configuration records, and the only call that places an order is `POST /api/orders`, which creates it unpaid. The connector puts that in `orderService.codCheckout()`, and leaves every capture unimplemented, because marking an order paid without verifying a payment provider’s signature would be a fraud hole.
limitations: The storefront cannot complete an order. Its payment step calls one method per gateway, and on CS-Cart each throws `NotSupportedError`; the connector’s `orderService.codCheckout()`, which does create an order, is not called by the storefront yet.

The connector signs every call with an admin’s e-mail and API key, taken from `PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_SECRET`. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor to the store can read both and use that admin’s API access.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the cs-cart connector is active but PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

faq.q: Can I run a CS-Cart store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: No. Shoppers can browse and fill a cart, but there is no shopper sign-in and the storefront cannot complete an order. The connector also authenticates with an admin’s credentials from `PUBLIC_` variables, which every visitor’s browser receives.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to CS-Cart?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/cs-cart-connector`, set `PUBLIC_CS_CART_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Why can’t Svelte Commerce complete an order on CS-Cart?
faq.a: CS-Cart’s REST API has no checkout resource. The only call that places an order, `POST /api/orders`, lives in the connector’s `orderService.codCheckout()`, and the storefront’s payment step calls per-gateway methods instead, which throw on CS-Cart.

api.surface: The connector calls CS-Cart’s JSON REST API, API 1.0 under `/api` for almost everything and the `/api/2.0` prefix for reviews through `/discussions`.
api.auth: Every call carries `Authorization: Basic` built from an admin’s e-mail and API key, with no token, cookie or session to capture or refresh; shopper sign-in is not possible, because every `authService` method that would establish an identity throws `NotSupportedError`.

calls.what: `GET /api/orders` with `email`, `user_id`, `status` and `company_id`, `GET /api/orders/{id}`, and `POST /api/stores/{company_id}/orders` (or `POST /api/orders` on Multi-Vendor) with `payment_id`, `shipping_id`, `products` and `coupon_codes`
`GET /api/payments`, read in one page and narrowed in the connector to active methods

rules: Every request sends `Content-Type: application/json`, GET included, because CS-Cart otherwise assumes `text/plain` and the request fails.

Every list call passes `items_per_page`, because CS-Cart otherwise uses the merchant’s “Elements per page” setting, and totals are read from the body’s `params.total_items`, which CS-Cart sends as a string like every other value.

Flags are sent as `Y` or `N` and statuses as `A`, `D` or `H`, so the connector filters storefront lists with `status=A`; product sorting is limited to the `sort_by` values `date`, `status`, `list_price`, `product`, `price`, `code` and `amount`.

Creating an order returns only `{ "order_id": ... }`, so the connector reads the order back with `GET /api/orders/{id}`; for a registered shopper CS-Cart ignores the posted `user_data` and uses the address on their profile.
